newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac calls African leaders to meet on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Chirac calls African leaders to meet on Zaire.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday urged heads of east and central African states to call a conference quickly over the rapidly deteriorating situation on the Zaire-Rwanda border.

"The worsening situation and unacceptable tragedies taking place impose the holding of a conference under the auspices of the United Nations and the Organisation for African Unity," government spokesman Alain Lamassoure quoted Chirac as telling the weekly French cabinet meeting.

Chirac said the meeting should discuss refugees, trying those guilty of massacres in Rwanda in 1993-94, guarantees for minorities in Rwanda and Burundi and international aid for the countries involved.
Chirac's appeal reiterated a long-held position by Paris that the situation needed a conference of heads of state of countries in the area of Africa's great lakes.

Reports from the area indicated on Wednesday that Zaire and Rwanda were moving closer to war after two days of trading artillery fire across their border and a Rwandan military sortie into Zaire's territory.

France has intervened militarily in the past in both Zaire and Rwanda but senior French officials currently insist a repeat of such action is out of the question and that the issues should be handled internationally.
